description: The one outline planner's pieces (src/english/outline-planner.ts, data/english/outlines.json): each piece is one move of a section's shape, said only where its facts hold and, where it leans on the sentence before it, only after the moves it names in `after`. Written by the Story lead from counts of real inaugurals (docs/research/first-evening-2026-11-24.md); no real President's words. The first evening's texts come first: the President's inaugural.

slots.term-left: the time left in the speaker's term, in words ("four years"), from the term's record
slots.theme-name: the speech's theme said as people say it (speech-outlines.json themeNames), from the planner's theme
slots.run-span: how long the economy's run lasted, in words, from the macro months (address-story.ts)
slots.the-disaster: the year's worst declared disaster as people say it after 'the' (outlines.json disasterWords), from the national events engine's row
slots.about: the policy question's spoken noun phrase (question-names.json)
slots.to: the policy question's spoken verb phrase
slots.law-name: the law in force or proposed, named (question-names.json law)
slots.other-side: what the other side of the speaker's stand wants done, as a verb phrase
slots.belief: the speaker's reason on the question, as a clause (question-names.json reasons)
slots.belief-sentence: the same reason as its own sentence
slots.today: how the question stands today, said from the speaker's side, as a sentence
slots.today-clause: the same, as a clause that ends the sentence
slots.the-vice-president: the Vice President by office and name, from the officials engine's seat
slots.president: the President, said by the said-as reader (role first, then pronoun)
slots.president-object: the President in the object case
slots.said: what the President's point was about, as people say it
slots.employer: the speaker's employer, through the said-as reader
slots.born-year: the year the player was born, from the birth record
slots.school-year: the year the player first started school
slots.school-place: the town the player first went to school in
slots.moved-year: the year the player's household moved
slots.finished-year: the year the player finished high school
slots.college-year: the year the player started college
slots.lost-office: the office the player ran for and lost, as people say it
slots.lost-votes: the player's votes in it, as a number
slots.state: the player's state, as a sentence says it
slots.president-name: the President's full name, from the officials engine
slots.we: the household members who watched and the player, as the subject of a sentence ("Joe, Ann and I")
slots.us: the same, as its object ("Joe, Ann and me")
slots.name: the person's full name, from the record
slots.surname: the person's family name, from the record
slots.date: the day as a news story says it
slots.quote: the line of the address a reader can quote, from the address's record
slots.body: the body that voted, as its record names it
slots.law: the bill or law by its name, never its number
slots.purpose: what the bill does, as a noun phrase from the bill catalog
slots.count: the vote count in words and figures ("3 to 2")

parts.text: My fellow Americans.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Fellow citizens.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Thank you, everyone.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: A few minutes ago I swore to defend the Constitution for the next {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The oath I just took is one sentence long. Keeping it for {term-left} is the job.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I've taken the oath, and from here on you get to judge me by what I do with the next {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Last November you hired me for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Last November you gave me this job for {term-left}, and today I start it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You voted last November, and as of noon today the next {term-left} are on me.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Prices have outrun paychecks for {run-span}, and nobody here needed a government report to know it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: For {run-span}, the grocery bill has grown faster than the paycheck that pays it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: More people are looking for work today than {run-span} ago.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The last {run-span} have been hard on working families, and I won't stand up here and pretend they weren't.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: There's more work out there than there was {run-span} ago.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I didn't make that mess, but for the next {term-left} it's mine to clean up.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: No speech fixes {run-span} of that. Work does.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I own my share of those {run-span}, and I'm not going to blame anyone else for them.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: How many of you have stood at a checkout in the last {run-span} and put something back on the shelf?
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Who here hasn't carried home less from the store these last {run-span} and paid more for it?
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: How many of you know someone who's been out of work for most of the last {run-span}?
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: That isn't your failing. Washington spent {run-span} looking the other way.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You didn't do anything wrong, and I'm not going to spend {term-left} telling you to be patient.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Some of you are still cleaning up after the {the-disaster}, and you deserve a government that shows up and stays.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The {the-disaster} this past year took homes and jobs, and the rebuilding isn't close to finished.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Think about the families who lived through the {the-disaster} this past year.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The cameras have moved on. For the next {term-left}, I won't.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The rebuilding stays on my desk for all {term-left}, long after it leaves the news.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: If you didn't vote for me, I'll spend the next {term-left} trying to earn your vote anyway.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To everyone who voted against me last November: I work for you too, every day of the next {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To the families still rebuilding after the {the-disaster}: the government you pay for is going to show up.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To anyone who has spent the last {run-span} looking for work: this government works for you now.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To everyone stretching a paycheck that doesn't go as far as it did {run-span} ago: I took this job for you.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To the people who sent me here: thank you, and keep an eye on me for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: A few minutes ago I swore the same oath {the-vice-president} took just before me.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Last November you hired me, and {the-vice-president} with me.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You turned up in {born-year}, which the government noted on a form.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You were born in {born-year}, and nobody asked you first.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: By {school-year} the state had you in a classroom in {school-place}. That's how the state says hello.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In {school-year} you started school in {school-place}, where the first lesson was standing in line.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In {moved-year} the family packed up {moved-from} for {moved-to}, because the economy said so.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In {moved-year} you landed in {moved-to}. {moved-from} survived the loss.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You finished school in {finished-year}. The diploma came with no instructions.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In {finished-year} you got out of high school with a diploma and no particular plan.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In {college-year} you started college, which is a lot like school with a bill attached.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: {college-year} brought college, because everyone said so with great confidence.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: That fall you ran for {lost-office} and got {lost-votes} votes. The winner got {winner-votes}. The voters were clear.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You even ran for {lost-office} in {lost-year}. {lost-votes} people voted for you, which beats zero.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: And now it's {start-month} {start-year}. A new President takes the oath, {state} has its legislature back, and {place} has been talking about all of it without you.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: It's {start-month} {start-year}. Washington has a new President, {state} has its usual problems, and {place} has saved you a seat.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: That fall came college, which is a lot like school with a bill attached. Welcome to {college-year}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: {born-year} is when the paperwork says you started. You didn't file it.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Somewhere in {born-year}, a clerk wrote your name on a form and called it official.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Your file opens in {born-year}. It's short, and the first line is the only one you didn't write.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Born in {born-year}, no vote taken.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The county has you down for {born-year}. Nobody asked what you thought of the timing.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Count back to {born-year} and you find the first day you were somebody's problem.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: By the end of {born-year} you had a birth record, a name and no opinions yet.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Who picked {born-year}? Not you. You just showed up and let the government catch up.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {school-place} had a desk with your name on it by {school-year}.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Ask anyone what {school-year} was like and they'll shrug. You spent it in {school-place}, learning to raise a hand before you spoke.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {school-year}: a lunch line in {school-place} and your first lesson in waiting your turn.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Before you could vote, you could be marked tardy. That began in {school-place} in {school-year}.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The bell in {school-place} rang for you for the first time in {school-year}, and it kept ringing.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: What did {school-place} teach you in {school-year}? Where to sit, mostly, and who got to pick.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {school-year} put you in a classroom in {school-place}, and the state took attendance.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: When {school-year} came around, {school-place} counted heads, and yours was one of them.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The boxes came out in {moved-year}. {moved-from} got a forwarding address and {moved-to} got you.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: You left {moved-from} in {moved-year}, and {moved-to} had to learn your name from scratch.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {moved-year} meant a new zip code. {moved-to} was the one on the new mail.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Nobody in {moved-to} knew you in {moved-year}. In {moved-from}, people noticed you gone.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: A truck from {moved-from} to {moved-to} in {moved-year}, and your whole address changed with it.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Then {moved-year} sent you from {moved-from} to {moved-to}, where you started over as the new one.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Work took your household out of {moved-from} in {moved-year}. {moved-to} was where the job was.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: With a job waiting, in {moved-year} you left {moved-from} and set up in {moved-to}.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: You walked out with a diploma in {finished-year}. The line stopped there and so did the plan.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {finished-year}: the last school year with your name in it. Then the calendar went empty.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: High school ended in {finished-year}. Nobody handed you the next thing.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Funny how {finished-year} felt like a finish line, and the road kept going on the other side.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: By {finished-year} you had the diploma. What it was for was left for you to figure out.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The last bell of high school rang in {finished-year}, and the afternoon after it was yours.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Class dismissed, {finished-year}. For the first time nobody had a schedule for you.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: You graduated in {finished-year}. The paper said it was done, though you weren't sure what was.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Your first semester of college began in {college-year}, and with it the first bill with your name on it.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: In {college-year} you took your name to a campus and found it printed on a syllabus.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: College was next. {college-year} put you in a lecture hall with a long list of things to read.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: You enrolled in {college-year}. The tuition arrived faster than the classes did.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Who had time for a plan? By {college-year} you were in a class or a line for one.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {college-year} meant a campus, a new schedule and another place that wanted your ID.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The same year, {college-year}, college started. Your calendar went from one empty season to a full one.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: That very year, {college-year}, you started college, and the schedule changed again.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: You put your name on the ballot for {lost-office} in {lost-year}. {lost-votes} voters wrote it, and {winner-votes} wrote the other one.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {lost-year} was your first race, for {lost-office}. You got {lost-votes} votes, the winner got {winner-votes}, and you got your answer.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The count for {lost-office} came in at {lost-votes} for you and {winner-votes} for the winner. That was {lost-year}.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Not every try ends in a win. In {lost-year} you ran for {lost-office} and finished behind, {lost-votes} to {winner-votes}.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Then there was {lost-office}. {lost-votes} people marked your name in {lost-year}, and it wasn't enough.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {lost-votes} to {winner-votes}. That was the count for {lost-office} the year you lost.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: {start-month} {start-year}: the oath, the speeches, and {place} still wondering what you'll do with it.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: It is {start-month} {start-year}. {state} is where you live, {place} is where you wake up, and today the story is yours to take over.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: So here you are in {start-month} {start-year}, in {place}, with {state} still turning on the news.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: The years behind you are done. {start-month} {start-year} is now, and {place} is the stage.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Enough history. It's {start-month} {start-year}, you live in {place}, and {state} won't wait.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: Everything before this was background. {start-month} {start-year} in {place} is where it counts.
parts.author: the before-and-around writer

parts.text: You sent me here in November to do a job, and I have {term-left} to do it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The campaign is over. You picked me in November, and the next {term-left} start now.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I just made a promise to this whole country, and I have {term-left} to keep it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: For {run-span}, the paycheck has gone a little further at the grocery store.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Washington has a short memory for places like yours. Mine will last {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Every family still waiting on help from the {the-disaster} is the first thing on my desk tomorrow.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In November you chose me, and {the-vice-president} with me, and today we both go to work.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: For the families the {the-disaster} hit, this past year has been about getting a roof back.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: A lot of families have a little more room at the end of the month than they did {run-span} ago.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Some of that rebuilding will take all {term-left}, and I'll be here for all of it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I'll go see it for myself before the month is out, and I'll keep going back for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Plenty of families are still waiting to get back home after the {the-disaster} this past year.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: More families can cover the rent and still put something away than could {run-span} ago.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: For {term-left} I answer to all of you under that oath, not just the ones who voted for me.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I raised my right hand a few minutes ago, and the job became mine for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The oath is short. The {term-left} after it are not.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Every President before me said the same words I just said, and each one found out what they cost over {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: As of the oath, the office is mine for {term-left}, and so is every hard call that comes with it.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The oath doesn't promise you a perfect President. It promises you one who answers to you for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: I swore to protect the Constitution, and for {term-left}, that comes before everything else on my list.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In November you made a choice, and I'm the result for the next {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You voted in November. Now it's my turn to show up for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: November's votes are counted, and today I start earning them for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: The election ended in November. The job starts today and runs {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: Last fall the country picked a direction, and I've got {term-left} to follow it through.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: You trusted me with your vote in November, and I'll try to be worth it for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: In November the votes came in, and now the work is mine for {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To the young people who voted for the first time last fall: the next {term-left} are yours as much as mine.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To everyone working a shift right now: I'm working for you too, for all {term-left}.
parts.author: the Story lead

parts.text: To anyone who's given up on Washington: give me {term-left} to change your mind.
parts.author: the Story lead
